channel.title: Nature Physics
channel.description: Nature Physics offers news and reviews alongside top-quality research papers in a monthly publication, covering the entire spectrum of physics. Physics addresses the properties and interactions of matter and energy, and plays a key role in the development of a broad range of technologies. To reflect this, Nature Physics covers all areas of pure and applied physics research. The journal focuses on core physics disciplines, but is also open to a broad range of topics whose central theme falls within the bounds of physics.

item.title: [8] Thermodynamic demonstration of tetracriticality and multicomponent superconductivity in UTe2
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Jörg Schmalian, B. J. Ramshaw

Authors: Sahas Kamat, Jared Dans, Shanta Saha, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important study on a major candidate for topological/unconventional superconductivity relevant to user interests.

Tags: #thermodynamics #UTe2 #superconductivity

Abstract: Prior measurements of the phase diagram of UTe2 contain a triple point that is forbidden by thermodynamics. Now, an additional phase boundary is discovered that resolves this problem and confirms multicomponent superconductivity in this material.

item.title: [6] Imaging hot-electron Thomson cooling beyond the Boltzmann–Onsager framework
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Wu Li, Zhenghua An

Authors: Xinrong Zuo, Guokang Zhang, Weikang Lu, et al.

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Electronic transport imaging in HgTe quantum wells, which are classic topological systems.

Tags: #imaging #HgTe #transport

Abstract: Classical Thomson cooling is inefficient. Now non-equilibrium energy dissipation with a breakdown of the Boltzmann–Onsager limit is demonstrated by imaging hot electrons in HgTe and HgCdTe quantum wells.

item.title: [9] A simple twist to altermagnetism
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Yingying Zhang, Cheng Song

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct hit on altermagnetism and twisted van der Waals structures, highly relevant topics.

Tags: #material #altermagnetism #vanderWaals

Abstract: Two-dimensional altermagnets hold promise for next-generation spintronics but remain difficult to synthesize. Now, altermagnetism has been observed in an orthogonally twisted van der Waals homostructure, opening possibilities for ultrathin devices.
